newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks firm, business to get lively.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks firm, business to get lively.

text.p: Most Croatian stocks closed the week on a firmer note after trade was slowed by a brokers' meeting outside the capital, but market participants predicted livelier business next week.

"I expect stronger trade and possibly a rise of all viable stocks," said Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage. "I don't see any huge leaps in prices but investors are definitely interested in buying larger share packages," he said.
"The atmosphere on the market is obviously positive after the bearish trend of some weeks ago," he said.
Friday's slow trading came after a boom on Thursday. Volume fell to 6,130 units from Thursday's 24,784 and turnover shrank tenfold to 3.4 million kuna.
Eight of 12 active issues rose on Friday, two fell and two were flat. Issues that had carried the market throughout the week kept a low profile.

Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka ordinary shares, which sold over 13,741 units on Thursday, did not trade. Its E-series preference stock stayed flat at 1,350 kuna but were the most actively traded stock with 1,271 units.
"Buyers may be thinking that the price of the bank's E-series should draw closer to the ordinary share," Nikolac said.
Fully-listed drugs firm Pliva inched up two kuna to 462, selling 1,194 shares.
Food concern Podravka lost one kuna to 288, with 977 shares sold but was firmer now after recovering from the level of around 250 kuna where it traded some weeks ago.
"Investors have confidence in the stock. It could rise further although it may be keeping a low profile for some days," Nikolac said.
